mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 50,000 units signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by more than 50,000 in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that accelerates wage growth and corporate profit margins, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE is below 5.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 0.2% and decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below 0.5% signals an overheating economy with supply constraints, prompting Federal Reserve tightening that causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when CPIAUCSL rises >0.2% and INDPRO falls >0.5% but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200.0 thousand units signals weakening real estate sector demand, reducing consumer wealth and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In FEDFUNDS > 2.0% periods, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST declines below 1200.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1220.0 thousand units signals strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST increases by more than 10% in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer credit (RSAFS) falls below 430,000 million dollars for two consecutive months, it signals reduced consumer spending power and weakening demand, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS is below 430000 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GDP (GDPC1) below 16300.0 billion dollars and industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 index signals economic contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when GDPC1 falls below 16300.0 and INDPRO falls below 100.0 but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery phase (UNRATE falling below 5.5% after a peak above 6.5%), a sustained decline in unemployment rate signals improving labor conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.5% after a peak above 6.5%
failure_condition: In labor market recovery phases, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
